protocol.name: AAuth
protocol.description: AAuth agent authorization (draft-hardt-oauth-aauth-protocol-11): five resource access modes, from agent identity to federated authorization, with shared fragments for obtaining agent and person tokens and for user consent.

entities.name: Person
entities.description: The human the agent acts for; approves missions and consents to access

entities.name: Agent Provider
entities.description: Issues agent tokens that bind the agent's signing key to its identifier

entities.name: Agent
entities.description: Holds a signing key and signs every request; identified as aauth:local@domain

entities.name: Resource
entities.description: Verifies signed requests, issues resource tokens and enforces auth tokens

entities.name: Person Server
entities.description: Issues person tokens and auth tokens; obtains the person's consent

entities.name: Access Server
entities.description: The resource's own policy server; issues auth tokens in federated access

tokens.name: Agent token
tokens.description: aa-agent+jwt, lifetime of at most 24 hours

claims.name: cnf
claims.description: The agent's public key; must match the key that signed the request

tokens.name: Person token
tokens.description: aa-person+jwt, lifetime of at most 1 hour

claims.name: aud
claims.description: The resource the token identifies the person to

claims.name: sub
claims.description: Directed user identifier for this resource

tokens.name: Resource token
tokens.description: aa-resource+jwt; aud is the PS in three-party access and the AS in federated access

claims.name: aud
claims.description: The PS URL or the AS URL

claims.name: agent_jkt
claims.description: JWK thumbprint of the agent's key, compared with the key that signed the request

claims.name: presented_jti
claims.description: jti of the token the agent presented to the resource

claims.name: sub
claims.description: sub of the token the request carried

tokens.name: Auth token
tokens.description: aa-auth+jwt issued by the AS, or by the PS in three-party access; lifetime of at most 1 hour

claims.name: aud
claims.description: The resource the agent may access

tokens.name: Session token
tokens.description: Returned in the AAuth-Access header; sent back in Authorization: AAuth, which the signature must cover

scenarios.name: Agent identity
scenarios.description: The resource learns which agent is calling and applies its own access control. Replaces API keys with cryptographic identity.

example.note: The agent signs every request with the key in the token's cnf; the verifier checks the signature against that key.
The resource decides on the agent's identity alone (sub of the agent token).

scenarios.name: Resource-managed access (two-party)
scenarios.description: The resource runs its own authorization, then returns a session token in the AAuth-Access header.

flows.label: Completes the resource's own login and consent

example.note: The session token is opaque to the agent and meaningless without the agent's signature.

flows.label: HTTP Sig w/ agent_token + Authorization: AAuth

example.note: The signature must cover the authorization header, so the session token cannot be replayed as a bearer token.

scenarios.name: Person identity
scenarios.description: Federated login for agents: the resource learns which person the agent acts for from a person token. The PS is not in the path of any call.

example.note: The person token replaces the agent token in Signature-Key. Its cnf is the same key that signs, so verification works as before.
The resource now knows which person the agent acts for: the pair (iss, sub).

scenarios.name: PS authorization (three-party)
scenarios.description: The resource has no access server. It accepts identity and consent from the PS that issued the person token.

example.note: The signature does not cover this body: Content-Digest is required only toward PS and AS endpoints, unless the resource asks for it through additional_signature_components.
aud is the PS (three-party: the resource has no access server). presented_jti names the person token the agent presented, and agent_jkt is the thumbprint of the agent's key.
The PS checks agent_jkt against the key that signed this request (the agent's), and checks presented_token against the resource token's presented_jti, ps and sub.
The PS issues the auth token itself (dwk aauth-person.json). Its exp does not exceed the person token's, so expires_in is shorter than an hour.
The resource checks iss, aud, cnf against the signing key, sub and scope.

scenarios.name: Federated authorization (four-party)
scenarios.description: The resource has its own access server. The PS federates with the AS named by the resource token's aud.

flows.label: POST auth_token_endpoint w/ resource_token (HTTP Sig w/ jwks_uri)
flows.note: The PS signs with its own key, while the resource token's agent_jkt names the agent's key

scenarios.name: Obtain agent token
scenarios.description: The agent proves its identity to its agent provider through a platform-specific mechanism and receives an agent token for its key.

example.note: How the agent proves itself to its agent provider is platform-specific (I-D.hardt-aauth-bootstrap). The agent token binds the agent's key (cnf) to its identifier (sub) for at most 24 hours.

scenarios.name: Obtain person token
scenarios.description: The agent asks its PS for a person token addressed to the resource.

example.note: A body sent to a PS must be covered by the signature through Content-Digest and Content-Type (§11.3.3.1). The draft's own example in §7.1 omits them.
The person token names one resource (aud) and a directed identifier for the person there (sub). It carries no scope.

scenarios.name: User consent
scenarios.description: The PS needs the person: it returns 202 with an interaction URL and code, the person approves, and the agent polls the pending URL.

example.note: The PS needs the person before it can issue. The agent sends the person to the interaction URL with the code and polls the Location URL.
Polling switches to GET on the Location URL and does not resend the original body. Prefer: wait asks the PS to hold the response until it can answer.
